claims.text: Nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 develops Cr-V-rich precipitates after irradiation to approximately 8 dpa.
The precipitates formed in irradiated W38Ta36Cr15V11 are associated with increased hardening.
Adding approximately 2 at.% Hf to nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 will suppress irradiation-induced Cr-V-rich precipitate formation.
Hf will preferentially segregate to grain boundaries and other defect sites in the nanocrystalline alloy.
Segregated Hf will retard the local diffusion of Cr and V.
Reduced Cr and V mobility will limit the nucleation and growth of Cr-V-rich precipitates during irradiation.
The approximately 2 at.% Hf addition will preserve the alloy's low irradiation-induced hardening.
The approximately 2 at.% Hf addition will preserve the alloy's radiation resistance.
The low Hf concentration will not compromise practical bulk manufacturability.
At approximately 8 dpa, the Hf-modified alloy will have a markedly lower density of Cr-V-rich precipitates than the unmodified alloy.
At approximately 8 dpa, the Hf-modified alloy will have irradiation-induced hardening similar to the low level of the unmodified alloy.
The intervention is expected to be effective up to approximately 8 dpa at specimen temperatures of approximately 300–500 °C.
Approximately 300–500 °C is representative of fusion first-wall or divertor service temperatures for this test.
The optimal Hf concentration and its irradiation-induced segregation behavior are not known.
The proposed comparison uses an undoped W38Ta36Cr15V11 control and an otherwise comparable alloy containing approximately 2 at.% Hf.
Failure to reduce precipitate density or size, or a significant hardness increase relative to the undoped control, would falsify the proposed precipitate-suppression and low-hardening hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial-state and baseline fields say that precipitates in the unmodified alloy cause increased hardening, whereas the mechanism and predicted-outcome fields characterize the unmodified alloy as having a low level of irradiation-induced hardening that should be retained.
